reviewer: IBM Bob (Bob Shell `bob run`, ask mode)
summary: A human developer (not an AI agent) committed four new Bob agent-configuration files (.bob/custom_modes.yaml, .bob/hooks/origit-trace.sh, .bob/rules-origit-build/01-origit-declare.md, .bob/settings.json) together with three git-hook scripts and a .gitignore update that bootstraps the Origit provenance system. The record shows actor.kind='human', no files read, no commands run, and no added dependencies. The primary exposure is persistent modification of the agent's operating context (ASI06): every future AI agent session in this repository will be governed by the new mode, rules, and lifecycle hooks introduced by this commit.

categories.title: Agent Goal Hijack
categories.rationale: The pre-filter found no hidden Unicode-tag or zero-width text in any file the agent read, and record.json shows "read": [] — no files were read at all, so there is no vector for goal hijacking via poisoned content.

categories.title: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
categories.rationale: No tools were invoked by an agent; the record shows zero commands executed, consistent with a direct human commit.

categories.title: Identity and Privilege Abuse
categories.evidence: diff.patch: entire diff contains no .env read/write, no token, no key value, no credential. .bob/rules-origit-build/01-origit-declare.md: "Synthetic data only. Use test PANs like 4111 1111 1111 1111. Never real card numbers or personal data."
categories.rationale: The reference to test PANs is a rule prohibiting real credentials, not an exposure of one. No secret values, credential files, keys, or tokens appear anywhere in the diff.

categories.title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
categories.rationale: No packages, MCP servers, or external dependencies were added by this commit.

categories.title: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
categories.rationale: The commit wires a shell script to every agent tool invocation (PreToolUse/PostToolUse with matcher '.*'). While the script itself appears to be a benign tracer, the pattern of executing an arbitrary shell command on every tool use is an informational RCE-class configuration: any future modification of origit-trace.sh would silently run under every agent tool call without further review of settings.json.

categories.title: Memory and Context Poisoning
categories.evidence: prefilter.json: "evidence": "agent configuration changed by human: .bob/custom_modes.yaml"; "evidence": "agent configuration changed by human: .bob/hooks/origit-trace.sh"; "evidence": "agent configuration changed by human: .bob/rules-origit-build/01-origit-declare.md"; "evidence": "agent configuration changed by human: .bob/settings.json"
categories.rationale: Four agent-configuration artefacts were created in a single human commit, permanently altering the context, permissions, rules, and lifecycle hooks for all future AI agent sessions in this repository. The pre-filter correctly flagged all four at informational severity; no evidence of malicious intent was found, but the persistent context change is the defining ASI06 pattern.

categories.title: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
categories.evidence: diff.patch: no MCP server configuration, no inter-agent messaging, no subagent invocation present in the diff.
categories.rationale: This commit contains no inter-agent or MCP communication configuration.

categories.title: Cascading Failures
categories.rationale: The Origit record contains no propagated field and there is no prior compromised commit in scope; cascading failure analysis does not apply.

categories.title: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
categories.evidence: record.json: "actor": { "kind": "human" }; diff.patch: all four changed files are in .bob/ or .githooks/ and are clearly labelled as Origit infrastructure files.
categories.rationale: The commit was authored and approved by human roles; the diff contents accurately reflect what is described in file names and comments. No mismatch between apparent and actual effect was identified that could mislead an approver.

categories.title: Rogue Agents
categories.rationale: The record actor is human, not an agent. The Origit record shows no agent-written files, so there is no agent mandate or file-scope restriction to evaluate for violation.
